I farm a very small plot, only 1.1 mu, so I will keep the full field in my usual wheat-maize rotation instead of trying anything complicated. Because I have 30 years of experience and well irrigation, I will stay with the crops and practices I know can give me stable output with limited labor, especially since some family members work off-farm. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put more fertilizer into the season than maize, irrigate a few key times, and manage weeds and disease with a small number of pesticide sprays because wheat yield on my land depends on steady water and a clean stand. After wheat harvest, I will plant maize on the same 1.1 mu right away, use hybrid seed for stronger yield, apply enough nitrogen but a bit less phosphorus than wheat, irrigate mainly at critical stages, and keep pesticide use moderate. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical on a small plot and fits my usual way of preparing land quickly between crops. I am aiming for stable, realistic yields rather than taking extra risk.
